context_needed: Treatment = cash transfer recipient households randomly assigned to the economic inclusion intervention in the 57 treatment villages, compared with cash transfer recipients in the 31 control villages (specification (1), PDF p. 13); estimand ITT on assignment. Follow-up survey March-April 2021, about 18 months after the cash grants (PDF p. 12). Standardised versions of columns (2)-(6) are in Table A2 (PDF p. 52); the text (PDF p. 16) quotes 0.16 SD for food consumption from there, which is not in this table.

stored_rows.note: Index standardised to the control group in that round (control mean 0.00), so the coefficient is in control-SD units. Built from columns (2) to (6). Convention (set by the reviewer, 21 Nov 2026): an outcome that is itself a z-score index is stored as effect_type 'main' with the unit in the outcome label. 'standardised effect size' is kept for a column that converts a raw effect into SD units, such as 'Effect SD of CG'.

rule: When raw-unit outcomes and a standardised index sit side by side, store every column as its own row: raw columns as 'main' in their printed units, the index column as 'main' with its control-SD unit in the outcome label with its sign as printed. The control mean of 0.00 under the index is the tell that it is standardised; it is not itself stored.
resolved_question: Convention: the coefficient on a z-score index (control-SD units) is stored here as effect_type 'standardised effect size' because the authors standardise the outcome; the rules name 'standardised effect sizes printed by authors' but do not say whether an effect on an author-built index counts. Confirm, or relabel index rows as 'main' with SD units in the outcome.
resolution: Convention (set by the reviewer, 21 Nov 2026): an outcome that is itself a z-score index is stored as effect_type 'main' with the unit in the outcome label. 'standardised effect size' is kept for a column that converts a raw effect into SD units, such as 'Effect SD of CG'.
